title: Harness Descriptor
description: The data half of a harness adapter: every declarative value a harness exposes, plus references to named code capabilities (transcript summary/denial readers, slug generation, shadow preflight). The write guard is pure data (the [guard] block) rendered by one generic engine. Authored as TOML (harnesses/*.toml), validated after transcoding to JSON. Cross-field invariants (transcript composition, guard/banner lockstep, slug/naming-rule agreement, vocabulary coverage, guard template contracts) are enforced by the Rust loader on top of this schema.

label.description: Kebab-case harness identifier, used in CLI flags, dispatch.json, and staged conditions.json.

skills_dir.description: Project-local staged-skills directory, `/`-separated relative to the repo root (e.g. ".claude/skills"). Optional: a harness without one cannot stage skills natively, so runs fall back to --no-stage (each SKILL.md inlined into its dispatch prompt) with a preflight warning.

additional_project_skill_dirs.description: Additional project-local skill roots the harness discovers for compatibility with other harness conventions. These roots participate in codebase shadow detection and opt-in exclusion but never receive staged skills.

config_dirs.description: Harness-owned config directory names (e.g. ".claude"). Feeds the staging sibling filter and task-repository baseline inclusion.

run.description: Run-option capabilities; absent fields take the baseline defaults (no guard, bootstrap and stage-name allowed without staging).

tools.description: Tool-name vocabulary by role, as the harness's transcripts and hook payloads spell them.

staging.description: Native skill staging: slug shape (template or named capability), naming rules, and prompt phrasing.

slug_template.description: Staged-slug format with {prefix}/{iteration}/{condition}/{skill_name} placeholders. Mutually exclusive with slug_capability.

slug_capability.description: Named code capability generating the staged slug (sanitization/truncation beyond a format string).

stage_name_pattern.description: Regex a stage name must fully match (declarative validate_stage_name).

stage_name_invalid_message.description: Rejection message; {name} is substituted with the offending stage name.

skills_block.description: Harness-native available-skills block: header + one item per skill ({name}/{description}/{path} placeholders) + footer.

transcript.description: Transcript ingest: the events file the CLI dispatch captures, one primary summary reader, and optional composable denial/session-surface readers. The primary summary is either `parser` (a named code capability for streams that need stitching) or summary outputs under `extract` (the declarative tier for flat event streams). A parser may coexist with an extract containing only `session_surface`; `permission_denials_parser` may accompany either tier. These composition rules are Rust loader invariants.

permission_denials_parser.description: Optional named reader for permission-denial evidence. It composes with either primary transcript tier; when absent, a named parser retains its historical bundled denial capability.

extract.description: Declarative extraction by normalized output: an auxiliary session-surface roster, equality-filtered final/ordered assistant text picks, a native session-id pick, a flat tool-item mapping, a token reduction, and a duration rule. Streams needing keyed cross-event joins or content coercion for their summary are named `parser` capabilities instead. Declare at least one sub-table. A surface-only extract requires a named primary parser. Dotted paths descend nested objects only (keys containing literal dots are unaddressable).

session_surface.description: Session skill/plugin roster from the last matching record that reports at least one configured array. Explicitly empty arrays are evidence of an empty roster; no usable matching record means unavailable. Auxiliary: it may accompany a named primary transcript parser but cannot stand alone.

where.description: Dotted-path-to-expected-string equality filter; omitted matches every record.

skills_field.description: Dotted path to the skill-id array; at least one of skills_field/plugins_field is required.

plugins_field.description: Dotted path to the plugin array. Entries may be bare name strings or objects; object entries require plugin_name_field.

plugin_name_field.description: Dotted path within each plugin object to its namespace/name; required with plugins_field.

plugin_id_field.description: Optional dotted path within each plugin object to its source/runtime identifier.

plugin_version_field.description: Optional dotted path within each plugin object to its version.

tools.description: Flat tool-item mapping: each matching record's item object becomes one tool invocation, in stream order.

where.description: Dotted-path-to-expected-string equality filter; omitted matches every record.

item.description: Dotted path to the tool object within the record; omit when the record itself is the item. Records where the path resolves to nothing or a non-object are skipped.

name_field.description: Field of the item whose string value is the invocation name; records without it are skipped.

skip_names.description: Names that are not tools (message/reasoning items sharing the tool event shape).

args_omit.description: Structural item keys excluded from args; whatever remains (key order preserved) is the args object, null when empty.

result_coalesce.description: Result = first present of these item fields (present-but-null counts), strings verbatim and everything else compact JSON.

final_text.description: Final assistant text: dotted-path string pick over matching records; the last match wins.

where.description: Dotted-path-to-expected-string equality filter; omitted matches every record.

assistant_messages.description: Ordered assistant messages: every matching dotted-path string becomes a transcript event.

where.description: Dotted-path-to-expected-string equality filter; omitted matches every record.

session_id.description: Native resumable session id: dotted-path string pick over matching records; the last match wins.

where.description: Dotted-path-to-expected-string equality filter; omitted matches every record.

tokens.description: Token total: over matching records, sum the required listed integer fields, subtract the optional listed integer fields, and clamp each record at zero. Missing or non-integer fields count 0; a record where no sum path resolves never turns an absent total into zero.

where.description: Dotted-path-to-expected-string equality filter; omitted matches every record.

sum.description: Dotted paths to the token counts to add up.

subtract.description: Optional dotted paths to subtract from each record's sum before clamping it at zero.

duration.description: Wall-clock duration from exactly one of: `field` (a millisecond value; last match wins) or `timestamp_spread` (last minus first RFC 3339 timestamp; needs at least two parseable matches). The exactly-one rule is a Rust loader invariant.

where.description: Dotted-path-to-expected-string equality filter; omitted matches every record.

surfaces_skill_invocation.description: Whether the transcript deterministically surfaces native skill invocation or exact staged-file access (false routes the meta-check to a behavioral-influence fallback).

skill_tool.description: Tool name of the deterministic skill-invocation event the `__skill_invoked` meta-check matches (default "Skill" — Claude Code's Skill tool; OpenCode declares "skill").

skill_arg.description: Argument of the skill-invocation tool that carries the staged slug (default "skill"; OpenCode declares "name").

skill_access.description: Deterministic exact-path access signature for a harness without a native skill tool. The named tool must complete successfully and its command argument must contain the task's exact staged SKILL.md path as a literal shell argument.

read_commands.description: Literal executable basenames whose successful invocation with the exact staged path counts as a content read.

guard.description: Write guard: the data the guard engine renders into the harness's native pre-tool hook surface and a deny verdict. The engine selects the install mechanism: json-hooks (default) merges a hook entry into hooks_file (Claude Code, Codex); opencode-plugin and cline-plugin stage an embedded JS plugin at plugin_file. Restricted to embedded built-in descriptors (the guard fails open, so a mistyped user descriptor would silently disarm it).

engine.description: Install mechanism: json-hooks (default when absent) merges hook_entry into hooks_file; opencode-plugin stages the embedded JS plugin at plugin_file; cline-plugin stages the embedded JS plugin directory's index.js at plugin_file.

hooks_file.description: (json-hooks) Hook-config file the entry is merged into, `/`-separated relative to the staged env root (e.g. ".claude/settings.local.json").

matcher.description: (json-hooks) Tool-name matcher the hook registers for; every hooked tool must be declared in [tools] write/patch/shell.

command_template.description: (json-hooks) Shell command the armed hook runs, with {exe} and {marker} placeholders (e.g. '"{exe}" guard "{marker}"').

hook_entry.description: (json-hooks) JSON template of the hook entry appended to the hook config's hooks.PreToolUse array, with {matcher} and {command} placeholders in its string values; authored key order is written verbatim.

plugin_file.description: (opencode-plugin/cline-plugin) Plugin file staged from the embedded JS template ({exe}/{marker} substituted), `/`-separated relative to the staged env root (e.g. ".opencode/plugins/slow-powers-eval-guard.js" or ".cline/plugins/slow-powers-eval-guard/index.js").

verdict_template.description: JSON template of the deny verdict printed on stdout, with a {reason} placeholder; authored key order is the harness's on-disk contract.

shadow.description: Live-source collision preflight plus an optional operator isolation assertion. A later layer may inherit preflight from a built-in; every fully resolved descriptor with this table must still provide it.

preflight.description: Named live-skill collision scanner: claude-plugins, cline-skills, codex-skills, or opencode-skills.

isolates_live_sources.description: Unverified operator assertion that every live source reported by shadow preflight is excluded from every initial and resumed eval-agent dispatch. Detection is retained as informational provenance instead of benchmark validity warnings.

dispatch.description: CLI dispatch guidance: command templates ({model_arg}/{guard_args}/{mode_args} slots) and the prose around them.

env.description: Environment defaults applied only to eval-agent dispatches. Later descriptor layers merge by key and run --agent-env overrides them.

guard_args.description: Extra args spliced into command templates at {guard_args} when the run is guarded (leading space included).

model_note.description: Sentence spliced into next_steps_template at {model_note} when an agent model was declared.

exec_template.description: Copy/pasteable single-dispatch command; <eval-root>-style angle placeholders are prose for the human.

manifest_template.description: The dispatch-manifest harness section; {exec_command} placeholder; ends with exactly one newline.

conversation.description: Native same-session continuation used by scripted multi-turn evals.

token_usage_aggregation.description: How per-turn token totals combine: sum (default) for independent per-turn usage, or last for cumulative native-session usage.

resume_exec_template.description: One follow-up dispatch command. Must reference <eval-root>, <outputs_dir>, {session_arg}, and {prompt_arg}; {model_arg}/{guard_args}/{mode_args} are filled like dispatch.exec_template.

plan_mode.description: The harness's native plan mode, entered for the planning phase of a plan_mode eval. Requires [conversation] and a {mode_args} slot in both dispatch.exec_template and conversation.resume_exec_template.

plan_args.description: Arguments spliced at {mode_args} for every plan-phase round, leading space included (Claude Code: " --permission-mode plan").

act_args.description: Arguments spliced at {mode_args} for every other dispatch — act-mode rounds, judges, responder consultations, and the lint probe — leading space included (Claude Code: " --permission-mode bypassPermissions").

plan_file.description: The file the harness writes its plan to in plan mode. Writes under root are allowed by the write guard and the stray-write audit; a plan-phase round that wrote one has presented its plan, and that write's content_field is the plan artifact. Omit when the harness writes no plan file; the responder then decides when the plan is ready.

root.description: Directory the plan file lands in; a leading ~ means the home directory (Claude Code: "~/.claude/plans").

content_field.description: The write tool's input field carrying the file contents (Claude Code: "content").
